interactions.summary: Jiang rejects the idea of God as a watcher and steers the class toward agency: the decisive movement is that people look toward God when they want salvation rather than being passively observed by him.

Jiang states the governing premise of the passage: God always welcomes and draws, but because the law of free will governs the universe, every movement toward or away from light is the person's own choice.

After a student says free will allows willing love instead of forced obedience, Jiang accepts that point as true but presses further on the deeper reason God gives free will, while another student offers a speculative energy analogy.

speaker_notes.note: The transcript compresses several clauses and briefly contradicts itself near the end, but the overall direction is clear: Jiang opposes surveillance and emphasizes free choice.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts the student's reformulation that the important agency runs from human beings toward God: people look to God when they decide they want salvation.
Jiang says God is always welcoming and always trying to draw people toward him, but the law of free will makes the human response entirely a matter of choice.
Jiang treats Dante's ascent toward light as an example of this universal law: you can embrace God and move toward light, or you can turn away and do what you want.
Jiang calls free choice the fundamental law of the universe and insists that everything a person does is chosen, even when it does not feel like a choice.
Jiang frames the packet's premise as the basis for Beatrice's continuing explanation across the heavens, not as a one-off side remark.

signature_moments.moment: God is always welcoming you, but everything is free choice.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's cleanest compression of Jiang's theology of invitation without coercion.

signature_moments.moment: Free choice is treated as the fundamental law of the universe.
signature_moments.source_phrase: This is the fundamental law of the universe
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns the classroom answer into a governing metaphysical principle for the whole lecture.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's name here for the universal law that makes each movement toward or away from God genuinely chosen.
The mode of divine action in this packet: God attracts and receives rather than surveils or forces.

chronology_notes.note: This packet resolves the prior watcher/tractor-beam tension by centering free choice, then leaves the deeper why-question open for the next exchange about why God would structure the universe this way.

uncertainty_notes.note: The energy analogy is a student's speculative metaphor, not Jiang's endorsed formulation, and should be reused only as an exploratory class attempt.
